finding: Tokyo core CPI accelerated to 2.7% y/y in September versus 1.8% in August and a 2.4% consensus, while the index excluding fresh food and fuel reached 3.0%, materially strengthening evidence of renewed Japanese inflation pressure after the BOJ's September hike.
net_new_delta: The prior ICARUS state centered on US duration and euro-area fragmentation. Fresh Tokyo inflation data add a distinct Japan normalization channel: inflation re-accelerated sharply above target/consensus and the yen strengthened, raising the probability that Japanese rates/FX can become an independent global-duration transmission factor rather than merely a recipient of the US bond shock.

evidence.claim: Tokyo core CPI rose 2.7% y/y in September, fastest in 10 months, versus 2.4% forecast; the index excluding fresh food and fuel rose 3.0%, strengthening the case for further BOJ hikes.
Japan's economy minister said Japan has emerged from deflation and does not require excessively loose monetary policy, while declining to prescribe the BOJ's next rate decision.
The yen strengthened after Tokyo inflation data supported expectations for further BOJ tightening while Japanese yields remained part of the broader multi-decade-high global yield environment.

conflicts: The BOJ Tankan showed mixed business sentiment and stable funding conditions, reducing pressure for an immediate additional hike even as Tokyo inflation re-accelerated.
Tokyo CPI is a leading regional indicator, not the nationwide CPI release, so national persistence is not yet established.
unknown: Whether September Tokyo inflation will be confirmed by nationwide CPI and persist beyond subsidy/base effects.
The magnitude of any JPY/JGB spillover into US Treasury term premium or NQ/MNQ is not established.
next_decisive_check: Confirm the signal against nationwide Japanese CPI and BOJ rate-path pricing; test whether JPY strength and JGB yield pressure persist independently of US payroll-driven Treasury moves.

oracle.finding: Add a Japan inflation-normalization state: Tokyo core CPI's jump to 2.7% with ex-food-and-fuel inflation at 3.0% warrants testing JPY/JGB sensitivity as an independent conditioning factor for global duration and NQ/MNQ rather than assuming US-rate dominance.

supermesh_x.finding: Reuters provided mutually consistent macro, policy-commentary and cross-asset confirmation for Japan while also surfacing a Tankan counter-signal; preserve Tokyo CPI, nationwide CPI, BOJ path, JPY and JGB evidence as separate provenance channels and do not infer a BOJ hike before direct policy evidence.
